aspects.says: A String switch with case null compiles to invokedynamic SwitchBootstraps.typeSwitch instead of a hashCode lookupswitch.
basis: section:A switch on Strings Is a hashCode lookupswitch Followed by equals
aspects.reason: the difference is in the emitted instructions only; the switch's results are the same, so a graded test of behaviour cannot see it

aspects.says: The class file holds only the concatenation recipe, so the running JDK decides the code; a class compiled for release 8 or with -XDstringConcat=inline keeps a StringBuilder chain.
basis: section:invokedynamic Leaves the Choice of Code to the First Run

aspects.says: The finally code is copied once per exit of the try plus once for the any handler, so a long finally in a method with many exits multiplies the method's bytecode.
basis: section:finally Is Copied Onto Every Exit, and a return There Replaces the athrow
aspects.reason: the copies show only in the class file's size and javap output; a method's behaviour is the same, and the practices' runner gives tests no javap to read

aspects.says: A concatenation or a lambda compiles to invokedynamic; its bootstrap method (StringConcatFactory, LambdaMetafactory) generates the code on the first execution of the call site, which costs milliseconds once, and later executions use the linked code.
basis: section:invokedynamic Leaves the Choice of Code to the First Run

aspects.says: Arithmetic instructions pop the right operand first: isub subtracts the top of the stack from the value under it, which was loaded earlier.
basis: section:Bytecode Works on an Operand Stack, So `i = i++` Stores the Old Value Back

aspects.says: i++ pushes the variable's old value before iinc changes the local, so i = i++ stores the old value back and an expression that uses i++ sees the value before the increment.
basis: section:Bytecode Works on an Operand Stack, So `i = i++` Stores the Old Value Back

aspects.says: javac copies the finally code onto the exception path, an any handler that stores the exception and ends in athrow; a return in finally is copied there too and replaces the athrow, so the exception is never rethrown.
basis: section:finally Is Copied Onto Every Exit, and a return There Replaces the athrow

aspects.says: A switch on a String switches on hashCode() and then compares every label with that hash using equals, so colliding strings reach their own case and a string that only shares a hash falls to default.
basis: section:A switch on Strings Is a hashCode lookupswitch Followed by equals

aspects.says: A null selector makes a String switch without case null throw NullPointerException from its hashCode() call.
basis: section:A switch on Strings Is a hashCode lookupswitch Followed by equals
